summary.headline: Sanghvi Movers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR277 crore; FY27 guidance reaffirmed at INR1,400-1,500 crore total income and INR525-575 crore EBITDA.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR277 crore (+32% YoY) with EBITDA of INR106 crore (+20%) and a 36% margin, while PAT was INR40 crore versus INR36 crore a year earlier. Revenue fell sequentially from Q1, which management attributed to renewable project phasing, monsoon slowdown in India and crane deployment timing in the Middle East. Order book rose to INR1,582 crore as of 23 October 2026 (+26% from INR1,253 crore in July), and the CFO said the book is executable within FY27 with about 8-10% expected to slip. Capex ceiling was revised to INR583 crore, with part of the KSA capex deferred to FY28 due to shipping and port constraints.

segments.name: Crane rental - India and Botswana
segments.commentary: H1 total income INR406 crore, fleet utilisation 78%, yield 2.24%, EBITDA margin 46%. Q2 India utilisation 71% vs 86% in Q1; yield 2.20% vs 2.04% a year ago. Segment DSO about 89 days.

segments.name: Crane rental - GCC (Saudi Arabia, Qatar)
segments.commentary: H1 total income INR39 crore, utilisation 86%, yield 3.80% vs 3.5% target, EBITDA margin 24% attributed by management to start-up costs. DSO fell to 165 days from 201 days in Q1.

segments.name: Renewables engineering and construction (E&C)
segments.commentary: H1 total income INR365 crore with EBITDA margin about 14%; TTM ROCE 63%. About 36% of H1 group revenue; FY27 mix now expected around 60:40 crane rental to E&C vs earlier 2/3:1/3. DSO below 60 days.

segments.name: Project EPC
segments.commentary: About 2% of H1 group revenue. Being wound down; management expects revenue recognition to complete in Q2-Q3 FY27 and to reverse the negative EBITDA shown on page 31.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reaffirmed: total income INR1,400-1,500 crore and EBITDA INR525-575 crore; management said the H1 result supports these numbers.
Management expects 8-10% of the INR1,582 crore order book (about INR140-160 crore) to spill into FY28, which it says keeps FY27 within the INR1,400-1,500 crore range.
FY27 gross debt to equity projected at about 0.70-0.75x, versus 0.72x ceiling cited earlier.
FY27 capex ceiling INR583 crore: INR182 crore capitalised in H1 (INR90 crore in Q2), about INR401 crore pending in H2, with capex typically back-ended to Q3-Q4 after monsoon.
Saudi capex of INR80-90 crore postponed to FY28; management expects GCC EBITDA margin to improve in the next full year.
Around INR120 crore of term-loan repayments due in H2 FY27.
Management expects Q3-Q4 yield and utilisation to improve, which it says will absorb fixed costs and average out margins.
Blended ROCE guidance for FY27 and FY28 given on page 18 of the investor presentation; management cites about 16% ROCE and about 16% ROE as targets.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex ceiling revised to INR583 crore including FY26 carry-forward; INR182 crore capitalised in H1 FY27 and about INR401 crore pending in H2. Management says about 96% of the planned pool is revenue-generating assets.
KSA capex of INR80-90 crore deferred to FY28 because of shipping, port congestion and delayed crane delivery; procurement is being aligned with contracted demand.
Management said it is waiting for shipping costs to normalise before mobilising some larger cranes planned for the Middle East.
Target yields: India about 2%, KSA 3.8-4%. Management said crane-level IRR is an internal metric and is not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Group order book INR1,582 crore as of 23 October 2026: India and Botswana crane rental INR683 crore, GCC crane rental INR45 crore, renewables E&C INR854 crore. Group enquiry pipeline about INR6,700 crore.
India H1 crane utilisation 78% within a historical 73-84% range; management expects H2 seasonal pickup after monsoon.
GCC yield fell to 3.80% in H1 from about 4% in Q1 because overtime work dropped in Q2 due to supply-chain disruption. Management said yields should recover next quarter.
Management said it does not pass cost escalation to customers in E&C; contracts are fixed price.
Management said it has framework discussions and MoUs with OEMs that establish it as an exclusive EMC partner (slide 24).

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR1,582 crore order book be executed this year, and could FY27 revenue exceed guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the book is executable in FY27 but E&C carries about a 10% deferral risk. Chairman Rishi Sanghvi reaffirmed guidance, citing grid, PPA, WTG supply, site availability and monsoon delays into Q3, and said 8-10% of the order book (INR140-160 crore) may spill into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East margin outlook given breakeven, and whether delayed capex could be brought forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the planned INR80-90 crore capex is postponed to FY28, the KSA business is EBITDA positive and generated cash profit in Q2, and margin should improve in next year's guidance. Shipping normalisation, which may take a long time, decides when larger cranes can be mobilised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the India crane margin fall from 53% to 46% when other income rose?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the one-time employee incentive was about 1% of margin and PF law changes plus insurance costs are the other operating cost drag. Management said contract labour costs will keep pressure on margin, offset by higher Q3-Q4 yield and utilisation. Other income includes an insurance claim on an impaired asset.

qa_highlights.question: Could Middle East strategy shift to India if the conflict persists, given GCC is only about 3-4% of order book and gross block?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the cranes are mobile and one 600-tonne crane was moved from India to KSA during the conflict. Management said GCC has about SAR216 million of live enquiries that it cannot service yet for lack of cranes on site. Gross block data is on page 29.

qa_highlights.question: How has E&C grown revenue over 40% while industry installations were flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman cited more than 20 GW of wind erection by the parent, full-scope services to independent power producers, and larger composite jobs. He said Sangreen Future Renewables has a strong order book, with the customer base reflecting the delivery record.

qa_highlights.question: Why did GCC yield fall to 3.8% from about 4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said lower overtime in Q2 due to supply-chain disruption in manpower and materials at site reduced yield. CFO said yield should rise in the next quarter, though he added 'ideally'.

qa_highlights.question: Are equity raises or a subsidiary IPO planned to fund expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said no equity raise is being considered at this point.

risks_watch: GCC execution and yield: shipping, port congestion and manpower shortages delay deployment; GCC EBITDA margin was 24% in H1 and yield fell to 3.80%.
Order book conversion: 8-10% of the INR1,582 crore book may slip, and the company flagged internal execution challenges in E&C.
Margin pressure from contract labour, PF law changes and insurance costs in the India crane business; India crane EBITDA margin fell to 46%.
Rising rates: RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps in October 2026, and weighted average borrowing cost is 8.28%.
Project EPC wind-down: management expects the negative EBITDA to reverse in Q2-Q3 FY27, which needs to be verified.
Heavy H2 capex of about INR401 crore, mostly in Q3-Q4, and about INR120 crore of term-loan repayments in H2 FY27; gross debt to equity is set to rise to 0.70-0.75x.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and visibility, but cautious on near-term execution: management reaffirmed guidance and called the Middle East deferral a timing issue. It was evasive on the India margin bridge, and on the INR9 crore PPE impairment, which it ties to an insurance claim booked in other income.
key_quotes: So as a management who believes in abundant and prudent cautious guidance, we believe that we still reaffirm what we have guided for between INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.
So shipping and port disruption in West Asia have delayed new crane deployment in Saudi Arabia, and we have moved part of the capex to FY28. So this is a timing issue, not a demand issue.
No at this point of time we are not looking to raise any equity.

adds.what: KSA crane capex of INR80-90 crore deferred to FY28 (shipping, port congestion, delayed crane delivery)
FY27 capex pool INR583 crore incl. FY26 carry-forward; INR182 crore capitalised in H1, about INR401 crore pending in H2 (~96% revenue-generating assets)

growth.why: FY27 total income guidance of INR1,400-1,500 crore (reaffirmed, not raised) implies growth that H1 total income of INR689 crore (+38% YoY) largely supports, with H2 backed by INR1,582 crore order book (+26% since July) and about INR401 crore of capex pending in H2, though India utilisation fell to 71% in Q2 from 86% and KSA capex is deferred to FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects Q3-Q4 yield and utilisation to recover from India utilisation of 71% (vs 86% in Q1) and GCC yield of 3.80% (vs about 4% in Q1), but India crane EBITDA margin fell to 46% from 53% on labour, PF and insurance costs, and group EBITDA margin is 36%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About INR401 crore of the INR583 crore FY27 capex pool is pending in H2, mostly in Q3-Q4, with INR182 crore already capitalised in H1 and about 96% of the pool revenue-generating, though KSA capex of INR80-90 crore slips to FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of INR1,582 crore (+26% since July) is executable in FY27 with 8-10% (INR140-160 crore) expected to slip, and H1 revenue grew 36% YoY to INR657 crore, though India utilisation fell to 71% in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 78% for H1 (India 71% in Q2) and KSA capex of INR80-90 crore is deferred to FY28 with no new capacity announced; management is still waiting on shipping costs before mobilising larger Middle East cranes, so a new capex plan is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 total income guidance of INR1,400-1,500 crore was reaffirmed, not raised, and management says 8-10% of the order book may spill into FY28, which caps upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 total income of INR689 crore needs H2 to deliver the rest of the INR1,400-1,500 crore range, while the INR140-160 crore order-book slip, GCC yield at 3.80%, and India margin pressure from labour and PF costs all carry risk.

rows.label: INR1,582 crore order book executable in FY27
rows.why: Book is up 26% since July to INR1,582 crore with INR854 crore in renewables E&C, and management says 8-10% (INR140-160 crore) will spill into FY28.

rows.label: Gross debt to equity rising to 0.70-0.75x
rows.why: Gross debt to equity was 0.58x at 30 Sep 2026, but H2 capex of about INR401 crore and about INR120 crore of term-loan repayments push FY27 gross debt to equity to 0.70-0.75x, against a 0.72x ceiling.

rows.label: Project EPC wind-down reverses negative EBITDA
rows.why: Project EPC is about 2% of H1 revenue and management expects revenue recognition to finish in Q2-Q3 FY27, reversing the negative EBITDA, though this is not yet verified.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, order visibility and reaffirmed FY27 guidance, and cautious on GCC shipping, E&C execution and India margins; analysts pushed on the India margin bridge, GCC yield, E&C growth and order book conversion.
